quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: When used on roadways, bicycles are considered:
questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?

options.text: If there is no oncoming traffic.
If the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot cross them to pass. You can only cross double yellow lines when turning into a driveway or business entrance.

questions.question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Braking on a curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: If you become drowsy while driving, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop at a rest area to nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills are not a safe replacement for real rest.

questions.question: When a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes loses traction on a slippery road, drivers should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Press down hard on the brake pedal and hold it, then steer to safety. The Anti-Lock Braking System automatically pumps faster than you could. Releasing pressure or pumping the brakes will turn off the system.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: There may be times when 10 mph is too fast for safe driving.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Drive slower than the speed limit when safety requires it. Bad traffic, weather, or visibility may mean driving as slowly as 10 miles per hour.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the speed limit, with caution.
Not drive more quickly than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when it rains, snows, or sleets. These conditions make roads slippery. You may need to drive slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: Highway signs that show hazardous conditions are called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. Obey them for your safety. Ignoring warning signs can cause accidents.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. They warn of upcoming hazards. This sign alerts drivers that wet pavement makes the road slippery and harder to control.

questions.question: Is it safe to pull in front of a large truck that is slowing or stopping?
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Do not pull in front of a large truck that is slowing or stopping. The driver needs the space ahead to brake safely. If you suddenly move into their lane, you reduce their braking ability and could cause a crash.

questions.question: When dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should slow down and turn on your:
questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: What does this white sign mean?

options.text: The railroad crossing is controlled. Drive at your normal speed.
Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the railroad tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, you must look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Let any trains pass before you cross.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
Your protected left turn is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left turn arrow means the protected turn is ending. You must be ready to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When passing a car, you have enough space to return to your lane when:

options.text: The other driver signals for you to move back.
You look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
You can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure there is a safe distance between your car and the car you passed before returning to your lane. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to move back.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol from your system. Nothing else—like food or caffeine—can speed up this process.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean passing is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions and no one can pass.

questions.question: Which of the following increases the risk of a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Cell phones (including hands-free phones) and any audio devices (radio or CD player) can distract you from driving and increase crash risk.

questions.question: Turn on your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days:

options.text: So others can see your vehicle.
To warn others of bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So others can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, headlights help other drivers see your car. If you need to use windshield wipers, you must also use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, you can pass only from the lane with the broken line.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves left then right.
The road curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right then left.
questions.explanation: This is a yellow warning sign with black markings. It tells drivers that the road will curve right first, then curve left. Slow down and adjust your speed safely.

questions.question: What should you do if you see an animal on the road?

options.text: Pass the animal as close as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Always be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly so you don't scare it.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give cyclists as much space as you can. Bicyclists are not protected like car drivers. Passing too quickly or too close can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: What should you do if your car breaks down on a highway?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers right away. Exit the road carefully and park as far off as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your car has a problem.

questions.question: How can you avoid drunk driving crashes?

options.text: Decide before you drink that you will not drive.
Say no if someone offers you a drink while you are driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving is to decide before you start drinking that you will not drive. Alcohol makes it hard to make good decisions, so plan ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes are about to become one lane.

questions.question: An intersection is blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the car ahead.
Do not enter the intersection until traffic clears.
Honk to make cars move forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if you cannot drive all the way through. Wait until the road ahead is clear so you do not block traffic.

questions.question: What should you expect if a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle?

options.text: The child will have complete control of the bicycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable. They may suddenly change direction. Bicycles and children are also small and hard to see.

questions.question: You exit a freeway on a downhill curved ramp. What should you do?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see what is ahead. Braking in a curve can cause your car to skid.

questions.question: What should you do when passing other vehicles?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to use a turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots before passing. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Re-enter your lane when you can see the front of the other car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: You may drive across a dashed white line:

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross them to change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when another driver makes an unexpected move.
questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Higher speeds require longer stopping distances. You need more time to stop when reacting to other drivers.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of roads with two-way traffic. A solid yellow line means no passing. A broken yellow line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow traffic laws and signals. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: A reduced speed zone is starting.
A reduced speed zone is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: A reduced speed zone is ending.
questions.explanation: The "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced school zone speed limit ends.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look for traffic, and go carefully.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your speed steady.
questions.explanation: When being passed, maintain your speed and do not go faster. Let the other vehicle pass safely.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull over to the curb or edge and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the curb or edge and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. On one-way streets, move toward the nearest edge.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead. This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: An orange and red triangular sign on a vehicle means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles like farm tractors and horse carts display an orange and red triangle on the back.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No. Driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes. It is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes. It is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. Driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive so slowly that you block normal traffic flow, you can be cited.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means right turns are not allowed. Do not turn right at an intersection with this sign.

questions.question: Highway hypnosis can result from:

options.text: Staring at the road for long periods of time.
Too much sleep the night before.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead without scanning around your vehicle. You stop paying attention and may crash into traffic that slows or stops ahead.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, you should:

options.text: Stop immediately and block its path.
Clear a path for it to travel.
Signal when it is safe for it to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clear a path for it to travel.
questions.explanation: Give emergency vehicles a clear path. Pull to the side of the road if it is safe to let them pass.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Slow down when the pavement is wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Reduce speed, avoid sudden braking or turning, and stay farther from the car ahead.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go the same direction.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line separates opposite traffic. Both directions may pass. Only pass if no oncoming traffic is in your way.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must do. U-turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means:

options.text: Turn after slowing and checking for traffic.
Do not turn until the light turns green.
Turn after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not turn until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. Wait until a green light or green arrow appears before turning. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time:

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Yield to the vehicle on your right. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: All motor vehicles in Maine must have liability insurance.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Maine law requires all vehicle owners and operators to have motor vehicle liability insurance. Every vehicle you drive must be insured.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If the fog is too thick to see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must yield to all drivers who arrived before you.
questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to drivers who arrived before you. Wait your turn to enter the intersection.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, what should you do?

options.text: Park with all four wheels off the highway, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the highway, if possible.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, park with all four wheels off the main road whenever possible.

questions.question: What should you do when the driver behind you wants to pass?

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver wants to pass you, slow down. This gives them enough room to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: When passing, when should you move back to the right lane?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead of the other car.
When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to the right lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This means there is safe distance between you and the other vehicle.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What type of drug is alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows nerve impulses and body functions, reduces your ability to concentrate, and affects your alertness.

questions.question: What should you do when entering an interstate highway?

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow to 25 mph before entering.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Use the merge lane to speed up and smoothly blend with fast-moving traffic. Do not stop as you would on other roads.

questions.question: When do large trucks lose speed most often?

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more time to speed up, so they lose speed on long or steep hills. Give trucks extra space, especially on hills.

questions.question: What should you do if a driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually to let them pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If tailgated, move to the right if possible. If you cannot, slow down gradually to encourage them to pass. Never brake suddenly as this increases the risk of being hit.
